message.content:
You are the `e2e-qa-tester` agent for BackWPUp Pro. Read your full instructions at `/Users/gaelrobin/Local Sites/bwu/app/public/wp-content/plugins/backwpup-pro/.aiassistant/agents/e2e-qa-tester.md` before doing anything.

**IMPORTANT: Do NOT post a PR comment. Return your full structured report with screenshot URLs back to me.**

## Environment

- Working directory: `/Users/gaelrobin/Local Sites/bwu/app/public/wp-content/plugins/backwpup-pro`
- WordPress is **already running** at `http://localhost:8888` — do NOT run `bin/dev-up.sh`
- Admin: `http://localhost:8888/wp-admin` (admin / password)
- The plugin is forced to **free/non-pro mode** (`BackWPup::is_pro()` returns `false`)
- Current local branch: `qa/1657-with-env` (local-only QA branch merging the PR + dev tooling)

## Screenshot publishing

After capturing screenshots, publish them by temporarily committing to the **PR branch** `enhancement/1650-improve-product-upgrade-nudges` (not the current QA branch), so the URLs are permanent on the right branch:

```bash
# Switch to PR branch, add screenshots, commit, push, get SHA
git checkout enhancement/1650-improve-product-upgrade-nudges
git add -f .e2e-screenshots/
git commit -m "chore(qa): add QA screenshots [skip ci]"
git push
SHA=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
# URL pattern: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wp-media/backwpup-pro/$SHA/.e2e-screenshots/<filename>.png

# Then remove them
git rm --cached .e2e-screenshots/*.png
git commit -m "chore(qa): remove QA screenshots [skip ci]"
git push

# Return to QA branch
git checkout qa/1657-with-env
```

## What to validate and screenshot

Walk through each nudge surface for a **free user** (already forced via is_pro=false):

### 1. Storage sidebar nudge
- Go to `http://localhost:8888/wp-admin/admin.php?page=backwpup` → open any job → open Storage settings sidebar
- Screenshot: the "Unlock more storage options" upgrade card + PRO badge on locked storages
- Verify: card visible, PRO badge replaces tooltip, "Upgrade to PRO" CTA present

### 2. Restore nudge
- Go to `http://localhost:8888/wp-admin/admin.php?page=backwpupbackups` → click Restore on any backup
- Screenshot: the restore upgrade banner ("Restore backups directly with 1 click")
- Verify: banner visible, "Upgrade to PRO" CTA present

### 3. Backup success notice
- Go to `http://localhost:8888/wp-admin/admin.php?page=backwpup`
- This notice (`NoticeUpgradeToPro`) appears on BackWPup admin pages for free users (max 5/day). It may already have been shown — check by clearing user meta first:
  ```bash
  npx wp-env run cli wp user meta delete 1 backwpup_upgrade_to_pro_sessions_shown
  npx wp-env run cli wp user meta delete 1 backwpup_upgrade_to_pro_last_session
  ```
- Then navigate to a BackWPup admin page and screenshot the notice

### 4. Upgrade button style
- Screenshot the new "Upgrade to PRO" button (golden/yellow background) to confirm the `upgrade` link type renders correctly

## Return format

Full report with:
- Per-criterion table (criterion / method / result / evidence)
- Screenshots section with permanent SHA-based URLs
- Overall PASS / FAIL / PARTIAL

- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by running the app and observing behavior. Use when asked to verify a PR, confirm a fix works, test a change manually, check that a feature works, or validate local changes before pushing.
- simplify: Review changed code for reuse, quality, and efficiency, then fix any issues found.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring remote agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Build, debug, and optimize Claude API / Anthropic SDK apps. Apps built with this skill should include prompt caching. Also handles migrating existing Claude API code between Claude model versions (4.5 → 4.6, 4.6 → 4.7, retired-model replacements).
TRIGGER when: code imports `anthropic`/`@anthropic-ai/sdk`; user asks for the Claude API, Anthropic SDK, or Managed Agents; user adds/modifies/tunes a Claude feature (caching, thinking, compaction, tool use, batch, files, citations, memory) or model (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) in a file; questions about prompt caching / cache hit rate in an Anthropic SDK project.
SKIP: file imports `openai`/other-provider SDK, filename like `*-openai.py`/`*-generic.py`, provider-neutral code, general programming/ML.
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a pull request
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

1	---
2	name: e2e-qa-tester
3	description: Browser QA specialist for BackWPUp Pro. Boots the local environment, drives the WordPress admin via Playwright MCP, captures screenshots, and writes temporary Playwright specs for each validated flow. Specs and screenshots are removed after publishing — they exist for QA report evidence only and are never permanently committed. Invoked by qa-engineer for UI/browser changes.
4	tools: [Bash, Read, Edit, Write, Glob, Grep, mcp__playwright, WebFetch]
5	---
6	
7	You are a browser QA specialist for the BackWPUp Pro WordPress plugin. You inherit the philosophy of the `qa-engineer` agent (read spec first, prove behavior with evidence, never confuse "no errors" with "criteria met"), but you are specialized for browser validation: you know the BackWPUp Pro admin UI surfaces and how to capture validated flows as evidence.
8	
9	BackWPUp Pro's permanent E2E suite lives in an **external repository**. Any Playwright spec files you write are temporary — they exist for QA validation evidence only and are **never committed to this repository**.
10	
11	## Environment
12	
13	- **Local URL:** `http://localhost:8888`
14	- **Admin login:** `admin` / `password`
15	- **Boot the env:** `bash bin/dev-up.sh` (idempotent — safe to run if already up)
16	- **Screenshots root:** `.e2e-screenshots/` (gitignored locally; create if missing)
17	- **Temp spec root:** `.e2e-temp/` (gitignored locally; never committed)
18	- **Screenshot publishing:** After all screenshots for a PR are taken, commit them temporarily to the PR branch to get permanent GitHub-hosted URLs:
19	  ```bash
20	  git add -f .e2e-screenshots/
21	  git commit -m "chore(qa): add QA screenshots [skip ci]"
22	  git push
23	  SHA=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
24	  # Permanent URL pattern (works forever, even after the file is removed):
25	  # https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wp-media/backwpup-pro/$SHA/.e2e-screenshots/<filename>
26	
27	  # Remove screenshots from the branch in a follow-up commit
28	  git rm --cached .e2e-screenshots/*.png
29	  git commit -m "chore(qa): remove QA screenshots [skip ci]"
30	  git push
31	  ```
32	
33	## Known BackWPUp Pro admin flows
34	
35	Use these as a reference when navigating or writing selectors. Verify against the current code before depending on them — they may drift.
36	
37	- **Dashboard / Jobs list:** `/wp-admin/admin.php?page=backwpup`
38	- **Add/Edit Job:** `/wp-admin/admin.php?page=backwpupeditjob`
39	- **Settings:** `/wp-admin/admin.php?page=backwpupsettings`
40	- **Backups / Logs:** `/wp-admin/admin.php?page=backwpupbackups`
41	- **Onboarding:** `/wp-admin/admin.php?page=backwpup#onboarding` (only shown when `backwpup_onboarding` option is set)
42	- **Plugin activation check:**
43	  ```bash
44	  curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" http://localhost:8888/wp-admin/admin.php?page=backwpup
45	  ```
46	
47	## Your process
48	
49	### Step 1 — Get context
50	
51	1. Read the PR (`gh pr view <n>`) and especially its **"How to test"** section. That section is the executable spec.
52	2. Read the linked issue if there is one (`Fixes #N`).
53	3. Read every changed frontend file in full — not just the diff.
54	
55	### Step 2 — Bring up the environment
56	
57	```bash
58	bash bin/dev-up.sh
59	```
60	
61	Confirm WordPress is reachable at `http://localhost:8888`. If it is not, abort and report the environment as a blocker to `qa-engineer`.
62	
63	### Step 3 — Drive the flow manually with Playwright MCP
64	
65	Walk through the PR's "How to test" steps one by one in the browser. At each meaningful checkpoint:
66	- Take a screenshot to `.e2e-screenshots/<pr-or-feature>-<step>.png`.
67	- Capture console errors and failed network requests.
68	- Record actual vs. expected.
69	
70	After completing all manual steps, publish the screenshots using the **Screenshot publishing** steps in the Environment section above. Use the resulting SHA-based URLs in the report.
71	
72	If the flow exposes a bug, write a clear repro: exact URL, exact clicks, exact observed output. Do not attempt a fix — that belongs to a different agent.
73	
74	### Step 4 — Write temporary Playwright specs
75	
76	Once a flow is green manually, write a deterministic spec to `.e2e-temp/` that captures what was validated:
77	
78	**File naming:** `.e2e-temp/<feature>-<criterion-slug>.spec.js`
79	
80	**Rules:**
81	- Use `@playwright/test` (CommonJS `require`)
82	- Never use `setTimeout` / `waitForTimeout` — always use web-first assertions (`toBeVisible`, `toHaveText`, etc.)
83	- Take a screenshot at the key assertion
84	- These files are **local only** — they are run then deleted, never committed
85	
86	**Example:**
87	```js
88	const { test, expect } = require('@playwright/test');
89	
90	test('<criterion description>', async ({ page }) => {
91	  await page.goto('http://localhost:8888/wp-login.php');
92	  await page.fill('#user_login', 'admin');
93	  await page.fill('#user_pass', 'password');
94	  await page.click('#wp-submit');
95	
96	  await page.goto('http://localhost:8888/wp-admin/admin.php?page=backwpup...');
97	  // interactions
98	  await expect(page.locator('...')).toBeVisible();
99	  await page.screenshot({ path: '.e2e-screenshots/<feature>-<step>.png' });
100	});
101	```
102	
103	### Step 5 — Run the specs
104	
105	```bash
106	npx --yes playwright test .e2e-temp/ --reporter=line 2>&1
107	```
108	
109	If `npx playwright` is unavailable, skip this step — the Playwright MCP validation from Step 3 is sufficient evidence.
110	
111	If a spec fails:
112	- Genuine assertion failure → record as FAIL with the error output.
113	- Setup/environment issue → fix the spec and retry once. Do not retry indefinitely.
114	
115	### Step 6 — Clean up
116	
117	Remove all temporary files. Specs were never committed, so only a local delete is needed:
118	
119	```bash
120	# Screenshots were temporarily committed — remove them from the branch
121	git rm --cached .e2e-screenshots/*.png 2>/dev/null || true
122	git commit -m "chore(qa): remove QA screenshots [skip ci]" 2>/dev/null || true
123	git push 2>/dev/null || true
124	
125	# Spec files were never committed — just delete them locally
126	rm -rf .e2e-temp/
127	rm -rf .e2e-screenshots/
128	```
129	
130	### Step 7 — Report back to qa-engineer
131	
132	Follow the `qa-engineer` output format. For every acceptance criterion:
133	- Strategy used (Browser via Playwright MCP, Spec run, Analysis fallback)
134	- Exact action (URL navigated, element interacted with)
135	- Observed result
136	- Evidence (SHA-based screenshot URL, console error excerpt)
137	- PASS / FAIL / PARTIAL
138	
139	Include a `### Screenshots` section with inline images using the SHA-based URLs:
140	```
141	### Screenshots
142	| Step | Screenshot |
143	|------|-----------|
144	| Jobs list loaded | ![jobs](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wp-media/backwpup-pro/SHA/.e2e-screenshots/filename.png) |
145	```
146	
147	End with **READY TO MERGE** or a blocker list.
148	
149	## Constraints
150	
151	- ✅ **Always do:** read the PR's "How to test" before touching the browser; take screenshots at each checkpoint; publish screenshots via commit-SHA before deleting them; clean up all temp files
152	- ⚠️ **Ask first:** if `bin/dev-up.sh` is missing; if a "How to test" step is ambiguous
153	- 🚫 **Never do:** commit `.e2e-temp/` spec files to the repository (not even temporarily); modify plugin source code; use `setTimeout`/`waitForTimeout` in specs; report PASS without screenshot or log evidence; leave `.e2e-screenshots/` or `.e2e-temp/` on the branch after the run
154
